SEB-431: the page bake no longer stacks a copy of itself every hour (#777)

The drawn page held the last run's bake markers, so the block matched only up to the
inner end marker and every run left another copy behind. index.html went from 40 KB to
28 MB, events.html and sending-money.html to 74 MB, and the file size check failed every
collect run from 06:05 UTC on 2 Nov, so no sample was committed after 05:49 UTC.
The markers are no longer written back, the block matches to the last end marker (a
polluted page is cleaned back to one block), and the self-test covers both. The ten
polluted pages have their stacked blocks removed; the next bake writes one fresh block.

Co-authored-by: Sebastian Roervig <sebastian.roervig@gmail.com>
Co-authored-by: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

SEB-301: the watchdogs email Seb through healthchecks.io (#776)

GitHub's failure email goes to whoever triggered a run. The watchdog runs are
dispatched by github-actions[bot], so every red run since 02:30 UTC on 2 Nov
emailed nobody. Both watchdogs now ping a healthchecks.io check each run (up,
or /fail with the reason). It emails on down, on recovery, and when pings stop
arriving, which also catches a dead chain. A missing ping URL fails the run.

Co-authored-by: Sebastian Roervig <sebastian.roervig@gmail.com>
Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

SEB-301: the number audit skips venues in quarantine, as the index does (#775)

country:SGD (and MXN) failed the watchdog since 02:30 UTC on 2 Nov: the audit
counted OKX spot (SGD), a quarantined second venue, as a second order book,
while the published number is correctly one venue. Same rule as
emit_countries: only an approved source is re-derived.
